title: Tensor coherence of the normalized scalar extension maps
statement: For any simultaneous normalized scalar and tensor-Hom models M [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data] and any family mu_a of ScalarHomTensorComparison, the two tensor routes for a:R→S and b:S→T agree: F_b(mu_a) followed by mu_b and tensor of the unit-normalized scalarHomExtensionComp maps equals scalarHomExtensionComp at the tensor followed by mu_(ab). For the identity ring map, tensor of scalarHomExtensionId inverse equals that inverse at the tensor followed by mu_id. These are equalities of actual derived tensor morphisms, without internal Hom or any flatness assumption. The full equations are the Lean attachment.

proof.text: Form the natural representative comparison epsilon from the scalar pair counit. The normalized transpose, applied to the ordinary chain unit, gives compatibility of epsilon with the ordinary and derived adjunction units on K-flat complexes with flat terms. Convert flatness using the ordinary/site tensor identification. Naturality along a K-flat resolution and cancellation of its localized augmentation extend this unit equation to every complex. Transposing it gives compatibility with arbitrary chain transposes. Retain the ordinary restriction composition and identity isomorphisms explicitly in the chain adjunction comparisons. Apply that compatibility twice, together with the generic exact-functor factorization equation for the canonical restriction composition, to show that scalarHomExtensionComp commutes with epsilon and the chain leftAdjointUniq comparison. The identity restriction factorization gives the analogous identity comparison equation.

proof.text: Use sheaf tensor generation and the total coproduct inclusions to test chain maps on total pure generators. The ordinary unit equation for the chain leftAdjointUniq composition sends the iterated scalar-unit section to the composite scalar-unit section. Naturality of the second unit, followed by the three given generators equations, proves the chain tensor composition square. For the identity comparison, its inverse is the chain adjunction unit; the same generator equation proves the chain identity square. These are calculations of the actual chain maps and require no flatness claim about an intermediate complex.

proof.text: On a pair of K-flat complexes paste the three given derived tensor normalization squares with the representative composition equation from step 1. Naturality moves the scalar representative comparisons and the tensor representative isomorphisms across the diagram; step 2 identifies the remaining chain routes. Cancel the source tensor representative isomorphism and the tensor of the composite scalar representative isomorphisms. The same pasting with the identity equations proves the identity case. Every derived object is isomorphic to the localization of a complex by essential surjectivity of Q, and a K-flat resolution of that complex supplies an isomorphic K-flat representative. Naturality along the pair of these isomorphisms extends the two equations to arbitrary derived objects.
